markdownDescription:
## Mascot Story Studio

Your brand mascot in a 15-second story for social — the same character, the same voice, a new story every week. Pickers fix the mascot's look, Voice Design fixes its voice, a product photo closes every episode, and the story is the only node you change to make the next one.

**Business use:** a brand with a character (a food brand, a farm, a kids' product, an app) that wants a steady stream of short mascot films for Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts without redrawing the character each time. The demo: a white lion, mascot of a strawberry farm, who loves strawberries — and finds the farm's crate at the end.

1. **Pickers + Notes + Product + Story** — Animal, Style and Render quality pickers, one line of notes (colour, age, what it carries), a photo of the product the story ends on, and this week's story; one image node turns the pickers into the mascot's character design.
2. **Story beats** — the mascot described from the design, the look, three scenes of two frames each — the last frame shows the mascot with the product exactly as photographed — the narration and the music.
3. **Character sheet → Frames 1–6** — the sheet fixes the mascot once; the six frames copy it.
4. **Timeline script → one take** — one prompt over the six numbered frames; one Seedance 2.5 node renders the whole 15 seconds in a single generation, silent, with the scene changes cut inside it.
5. **Voice + score → mix** — sound is added once, at the end: Voice Design speaks the narration in the mascot's voice; Suno writes one score; Merge lays both under the take.

1. Pickers + Notes + Product + Story — pick the animal, the art style and the render quality, add one line of notes (colour, age, what it carries), upload the product the story ends on, and write this week's story. One image node turns the pickers into the mascot's character design.
2. Story beats — the mascot described from the design, the look, three scenes of two frames each — the last one ends on the product — the narration and the music.
3. Character sheet → Frames 1–6 — the sheet fixes the hero once; the six frames copy it.
4. Timeline script → one take — one prompt over the six numbered frames; one Seedance 2.5 node renders the whole 15 seconds, silent.
5. Voice + score → mix — sound is added once, at the end: Voice Design speaks the narration in a creature voice; Suno writes one score; Merge lays both under the take.

data.title: Mascot story studio — how it works

data.text: Animal, Style and Render quality are picker nodes: the Character design prompt places each one by name — {Animal}, {Style}, {Render quality} — and every tile you pick becomes a line of prompt. Pick once, and every story keeps the same mascot; swap a tile — lion to fox, 3D to watercolour — and the whole series follows. The notes add what pickers can't: colour, age, what it carries.
data.label: Step 1
data.title: 1 · Design the mascot with pickers

data.text: The story in a few lines: what the mascot wants, where it goes, how it ends — usually with what you sell. The beats keep your events and your ending. Change only this node to make the next episode.
data.label: Step 1
data.title: 1 · This week's story

data.text: Three scenes, two frames each, narration and music. The two frames of a scene share the place, the light and the camera — they differ only by what the hero does in five seconds. Edit a frame by hand and rerun from it.
data.label: Step 2
data.title: 2 · Story beats

data.text: The sheet fixes the hero once; the six frames copy it. Rerun one frame alone for another take.
data.label: Step 3
data.title: 3 · Character sheet + Frames 1–6

data.text: A director turns the beats into one prompt — "0-5s: opens on @Image 1 … settles into @Image 2, cut to @Image 3 …" — and ONE Seedance 2.5 node receives the six frames as references in order and renders the whole 15 seconds in a single generation, silent. The two scene changes are cuts the model makes itself, so grade and light stay matched. Never render scenes as separate clips and glue them: the joins never match, and a per-clip soundtrack jumps at every cut.
data.label: Step 4
data.title: 4 · Timeline script → One take

data.text: Sound is added once, at the end, over the whole film. The narration is lifted from the beats in the hero's own words, and Voice Design speaks it with a creature voice built from one line of description — change the line to change the voice: a growl, a squeak, an old storyteller. A one-sentence brief goes to Suno, and Trim cuts the score to 15 seconds. Merge lays the voice (loud) and one score (quieter) under the take.
data.label: Step 5–6
data.title: 5 · The hero's voice + Score → Mix

data.label: Character design
data.prompt: Character design of the hero of a short animated film. The animal: {Animal || a lion.} Art style: {Style || 3D animation.} Rendering: {Render quality || high-end render.} Details: {Character notes || a small brave animal.} Full body, standing, centred, facing the camera with a gentle expression, on a simple clean pale background with soft studio light; high detail, appealing, expressive face. Exactly one character; no text, no logo.

data.text: The lion who loved strawberries. Every lion in the pride loved meat; this one loved strawberries, and he had only ever tasted one, found by a river. One afternoon he sits apart from the pride with that single strawberry, and decides to find where they grow. One afternoon he sets out — across the savanna, into a forest where the low sun cuts through the trees — following the smell. At sunset he steps out of the trees onto a hill and sees a whole valley of strawberry fields below. He lies down among the strawberries and eats until his muzzle is red, happier than any lion has ever been — and there, at the edge of the field, stands the farmer's wooden crate of strawberries, the best he has ever tasted.
data.label: Your story
Story beats
data.userInput: Story: {Your story || a small hero sets out to find the one thing it loves.} The first reference image is the hero's character design; the second is the product the story ends on. Write the story beats.
data.systemPrompt:
You turn a short story, a character design image of its hero (the first reference image) and a product photo (the second reference image) into a 15-second film of three scenes in three places. The film is a brand story: it ENDS on the product. Each scene is ONE five-second shot built from two still frames in the SAME place: the shot starts on its first frame and lands exactly on its second — Scene 1 runs from Frame 1 to Frame 2, Scene 2 from Frame 3 to Frame 4, Scene 3 from Frame 5 to Frame 6. Between scenes the film cuts. Write in exactly this shape, plain English, nothing else:
Character: <60 to 90 words describing the hero exactly as the design image shows it — species or kind, colours, markings, eyes, any object it carries, how it moves; this description is copied into every frame>
Look: <one paragraph of 40 to 60 words: the rendering style of the design image (illustrated, painterly, 3D animation — name it as you see it), the light, the palette, the lens — one look every frame follows>
Scene 1 — <place, time of day>:
Frame 1 — start: Image: <40 to 60 words: the still — the hero, its pose and expression, the place, the light, the camera>
Frame 2 — end: Image: <40 to 60 words: the same place and camera set-up five seconds later — the hero has done one thing (stood up, walked a few steps, turned, lain down)>
Scene 2 — <place, time of day>:
Frame 3 — start: Image: <…>
Frame 4 — end: Image: <…>
Scene 3 — <place, time of day>:
Frame 5 — start: Image: <…>
Frame 6 — end: Image: <the hero WITH the product, exactly as the product photo shows it — the same crate, box or pack, its colours and label — placed naturally in the scene; this is the film's last picture>
Narration: <three short sentences, one per scene, between 18 and 21 words in all and at least 100 characters — the HERO tells its own story in the first person (I), past tense, warm, simple words a child would follow; it must be spoken comfortably inside 11 seconds>
Music: <one sentence: genre, mood, tempo, instruments of the instrumental score>
Rules: the three scenes are three different places — beginning, journey, arrival at the product; the product appears only in Scene 3, and Frame 6 must show it clearly next to the hero; within a scene the two frames share the place, the light and the camera set-up, and differ only by what the hero does in five seconds (a few steps, a turn, standing up, lying down) — never a different spot, never a different hour; the whole story happens in ONE continuous stretch of light — the light may deepen from afternoon to sunset, but never jumps from night to day; the hero is the only character, nothing else has a face; describe any mess from food as juice or crumbs of that food, never as red smears or stains; no text, no logo; the story is the user's — keep its events and its ending.

Timeline script
data.userInput: Story beats: {Story beats || a six-frame story.} Write the video prompt.
data.systemPrompt:
You write the single prompt for a video model that animates one continuous 15-second film from SIX reference images attached in this order: @Image 1 and @Image 2 are the start and end of Scene 1, @Image 3 and @Image 4 of Scene 2, @Image 5 and @Image 6 of Scene 3 — the same hero, three places. You get the story beats. Write ONE prompt of 160 to 230 words in this order, plain prose, no headings:
First one sentence: the medium and look, taken from the beats' Look, and the hero once as it appears in @Image 1.
Then three gap-free timed intervals, exactly: "0-5s: …" "5-10s: …" "10-15s: …". Each interval opens by naming its start image ("opens on @Image 1"), describes the one thing the hero does in these five seconds so that the picture arrives at its end image ("and settles into @Image 2"), names one gentle camera move, and passes to the next scene with a clean, matched cut ("cut to @Image 3") — same grade, same light, the hero in the same mood. The 10-15s interval ends with: "The picture settles and holds on @Image 6 — the hero with the product, exactly as in @Image 6 — until the end."
Then the constraints as one sentence: the hero keeps its exact look from the images; it is the only character; no dissolves, no morphing between places — cuts only at the two scene changes; no on-screen text, no logo; silent — no music, no voice.
Output only the prompt.

data.label: The film
data.prompt: {Timeline script || One continuous 15-second film: opens on @Image 1 and settles into @Image 2, cut to @Image 3 and settles into @Image 4, cut to @Image 5 and holds on @Image 6; the hero keeps its exact look; silent.}
